title: PostgreSQL NULLS FIRST / NULLS LAST Index Semantics
realWorldScenario: A pagination endpoint sorts orders by `shipped_at DESC NULLS LAST` to display the most recently shipped orders first and pending unshipped orders at the end. Despite having an index on `(shipped_at DESC)`, the query takes 1.2 seconds and shows `Sort Method: external merge Disk` in the plan.
questionStatement: Explain how PostgreSQL indexes store NULL values by default in B-Trees. What is the difference between `NULLS FIRST` and `NULLS LAST`? Why did the index on `(shipped_at DESC)` fail to eliminate the explicit sort, and what exact index definition matches `ORDER BY shipped_at DESC NULLS LAST`?
expectedConcepts: B-Tree physical sort ordering and NULL placement
Default rules: ASC defaults to NULLS LAST; DESC defaults to NULLS FIRST
Sort elimination requirement: index ordering must match query ORDER BY exactly
CREATE INDEX ... DESC NULLS LAST syntax
hints: What is the default NULL placement for DESC indexes in PostgreSQL?
If the query specifies NULLS LAST but the index was built with NULLS FIRST, can the planner eliminate the sort?
Define the index with explicit DESC NULLS LAST.
